1.why: Set spreads one contrast, one restatement, one time and one causal; the causal 'Thus,' is the only one that carries a conclusion, which these items usually want.

2.why: Four identical sentences differing only in friction figures — nothing in the option text distinguishes them, so a middle pair was taken as a guess.

3.why: 'Instead,' needs a rejected alternative and 'In short,' a summary; 'Nevertheless,' is the general-purpose concession the set is built around.

4.why: Guessed on the predictor: 'enclosure temperature swings' is the most mechanism-specific of the four, but the numbers alone give nothing.

5.why: 'Meanwhile,' and 'In addition,' are additive filler and 'To be sure,' is a concession; only 'Consequently,' asserts a result.

6.why: All four state the same trade-off with shifted numbers; no textual discriminator, guessed.

7.why: 'For instance,' is the only option that introduces a supporting case rather than adding, contrasting, or concluding.

8.why: With 'For example,' and 'On the other hand,' both plausible fillers, the causal 'Hence,' is the one that needs a specific prior claim.

9.why: 'Still,' is the concessive holdout against an example, a time marker and a substitution.

10.why: 'coverage in an untreated pond nearby held steady near 40 percent' is the clean control; B and C have the control rising and D barely changing, muddying the contrast.

11.why: 'Instead,' is the only option that signals a corrected alternative; the other three are additive, concessive or restating.

12.why: 'only on Saturday mornings, the market's busiest period' plus 'could not record whether a passerby actually bought anything' names two real biases rather than one incidental gap.

13.why: 'the dust that settled was pale and coarse, blocking little of the incoming light' explains why the panels lost less output; the others explain dust removal, not a smaller effect from dust present.

14.why: 'the raised beds sitting along a sunnier south wall' is the confound that most directly undercuts the yield claim, matching a cautious summary.

15.why: 'By comparison,' is the only explicit comparison marker; 'In that case,' and 'Regardless,' both need setups the other options do not imply.

16.why: Additive, causal and specifying options crowd the set; the lone contrast 'However,' is the distinct function.

17.why: 'Granted,' and 'Beforehand,' are odd fits and 'By comparison,' needs two parallel cases; 'As a result,' is the plain causal.

18.why: Against a result, a specification and a plain 'Also,', the concessive 'Even so,' is the only pivot.

19.why: 'Even then,' 'Regardless,' and 'If so,' all need a stated condition; 'In practice,' contrasts theory with reality without one.

20.why: 'For example,' is the illustration option in a set otherwise made of time, contrast and consequence markers.

21.why: 'By contrast,' is the direct opposition marker; 'Nevertheless,' concedes rather than contrasts and 'If so,' needs a hypothetical.

22.why: Contrast, substitution and conditional-negative are all covered by the distractors, leaving the additive 'What is more,'.

23.why: 'Specifically,' narrows to detail, the one move not covered by the parallel, concessive and causal options.

24.why: Example, intensifier and similarity all point the same direction; 'However,' is the lone reversal.
